title: Schooling at Southern and Wilberforce, and his first song
summary: He attended Xavier, Southern and Wilberforce, was suspended over baked potatoes, worked as a mason, and first played Brown Skin, Who You For.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, I saw in one of the books that you went to Xavier.

To Xavier before. Yes, that's when... In... In... In... In... In... Grammar school. I see. Yeah, so naturally, in high school, I went to Wilcox. But in Southern, was it just around seventh, eighth grade, something like that. It's Southern University, just in high school. Starting high school. Mm-hmm. So I went to Southern. The funny thing about Southern... I went up to Southern. The president of Southern that later became Southern, he was in my class. The son of the president that was there then. There's only two buildings on the campus. It's a big city now. He and I were... Some other boys, friend, was the president's son. Three, four, five, or six of us were on there baking potatoes and fire outside of the dormitory. And the dean came up there and caught us baking potatoes. He said, what are you doing with fire on this campus? You're not supposed to build fire? He said, well, we were just sitting here. He said, what do you got here? He said, potatoes in the fire. Uh-huh. He stole them out of that barn right there. He said, I don't know. He was stealing. They were sticking out. The barn was just, you know, encouraging a few of them to fall out. But we didn't go in to get them. They were right there. There's a hole in the sea. And so they brought us before the faculty, or what you might call it. And they found out I was 13 when I came in. So they suspended me for two months. So I said, so eventually I could finish. But I went to Wilberforce University after that with my brother. Wilberforce Mama wanted us to be watched over by Otis, my brother, my oldest brother. And I said, well, that's my education. I didn't go to, I didn't finish college. But finished Brickland. I was a finished Mason. And made, of 11, I made, finished this before, a year before the German's time, at least three years. I finished two. Mm. Brickland. And California, when they were throwing bricks and building walls 24 inches wide, a big apartment house during the boom. And naturally, my dad came out later, and I worked for him. But I worked it to the tempest I could play music at night. I never stopped that. Music kept, was my goal. Well, ever since I first learned it here in New York, it's my cousin. He showed the first song that I played was Brown Skin, Who You For? You Showed It Look Good To Me. That was the first song. We've got the sheet music to that. Huh? We've got the sheet music to that. I didn't have it. We just played it by ear. That was the song they were singing around town. Brown Skin, Who You For? Showed It Look Good To Me. Yeah, that was it. Brown Skin, Who You For? Showed It Look Good To Me. Blue Tears. Bum, bum, dum, dum, dum, dum. Bum, dum, Brown Skin, Who You For? Showed It Look Good To Me. Yeah, I think that's it. Yeah, so that was the... I think I'll make a disco right now.
